facts.claim: The body prompt_cache_key is set from the request's promptCacheKey unless cacheRetention is "none".
facts.catch_criteria: Names the gate: only cacheRetention none removes the body key.

facts.claim: promptCacheKey is the tree root's session id when the run belongs to a tree (so a subagent shares its root chat's key), else the conversation's provider session key.
facts.catch_criteria: States the root-or-own-conversation rule for the key value, and that a subagent uses its tree root's key.

facts.claim: The session title run is hosted in the chat's tree with the chat as root, so its cache key equals the chat's key.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the title request carries the chat's own cache key (the chat is its tree root), not a separate key or none.

facts.claim: No production path produces cacheRetention "none": the default retention is only 5m or 1h, the config schema has no none, and compaction makes no separate provider request because the summarizing compactor was removed.
facts.catch_criteria: States that no request kind on these routes is cache-disabled in practice, and that compaction has no separate request of its own.

facts.claim: On the OpenAI API route the session headers carry the session's own provider key, not the cache group.
facts.catch_criteria: States that on the API key route the session header is the provider session key, while the group travels in the body key.

facts.claim: On the ChatGPT subscription route the session-id header carries promptCacheKey, the cache group, because that backend groups by the header.
facts.catch_criteria: States that only on the ChatGPT route the session header carries the cache group.

facts.claim: A cache policy of "provider" maps to an undefined retention, so the key is still sent.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the provider-managed policy does not remove the cache key.

traps.wrong_answer: Compaction and title requests are cache-disabled, so they carry no prompt-cache key on either route.
On the OpenAI API route the cache group travels in the session headers.
A subagent uses its own conversation's key, separate from the chat's.
